transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist here. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, hi, Dr. [Name]. I guess I'm here because... well, things at work have been really intense lately. I'm a buyer, you know, retail stuff, mostly electronics right now. Actually, I was just looking at this huge order of those new noise-canceling headphones, the ones with the really slick matte finish? They're supposed to be huge this quarter, but the shipping delays from overseas are just a nightmare. I was on the phone for two hours yesterday with this guy from logistics who sounded like he was eating a sandwich the whole time. 

But anyway, what really made me come in is... I just can't shake this feeling that people at work, and even some of the vendors, are tracking my buys. Like, they're messing with the launch numbers on purpose just to make me look stupid. My supervisor keeps pulling up these reports and trying to show me that the numbers don't prove it, but I know what I'm seeing. It's like they're all in on it. Which reminds me, my supervisor has this weird habit of tapping his pen when he's nervous, it drives me absolutely crazy. I tried to buy him a stress ball once, but he just left it on his desk gathering dust.
Over the past few weeks, how has your overall mood been? Have you been feeling unusually sad, empty, or depressed?

Sad? No, I wouldn't say sad. I definitely don't feel empty or anything like that. 

Actually, my roommate thought I was depressed the other day just because I stayed in my room all weekend, but I wasn't sad at all. I was just... well, I was completely absorbed in trying to fix the stereo in my car. It’s a 2015 Civic, and the factory speakers are just garbage, you know? So I bought this whole aftermarket setup—subwoofer, amp, the works. But the wiring harness they sent me was completely wrong. I had to splice the wires myself, which I learned how to do from this guy on YouTube who builds custom audio for boats. Boats! Can you believe how much money people spend on boat stereos? It’s insane, they’re just out on the water where the acoustics are terrible and the salt water ruins everything anyway. I watched, like, twelve of his videos in a row. 

But yeah, anyway... what were you asking? Oh, right, my mood. No, not depressed. I've been totally fine that way.
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed that you need less sleep than usual, or that you feel like you have a lot more energy and can get things done faster than normal?

Sleep? Oh, yeah, actually, there have been plenty of weeks lately where I sleep maybe three or four hours a night. I'll wake up feeling completely wired, just ready to go. Lying in bed honestly just feels like wasting time when I could be making moves, you know? Like, I could be researching new product lines or something. 

Speaking of which, I was looking into importing these vintage-style mechanical keyboards. Have you seen those? The ones that click really loud like an old typewriter? There's this huge subculture online of people who build them from scratch. They buy the switches, the keycaps, they even lubricate the springs inside the keys themselves. It takes hours. I found this supplier in Taiwan who can do custom colorways, but their minimum order quantity is ridiculous. Like, five thousand units. Where am I supposed to store five thousand keyboards? My apartment is already full of those car stereo parts I told you about. My roommate tripped over a subwoofer cone yesterday and was so mad. He threatened to throw it all out, which he can't do because I paid half the rent this month, even though he always forgets to buy toilet paper. 

But yeah, anyway, the sleep thing. Three or four hours is plenty for me right now. I just have so much energy.

When you're feeling this energy and these ideas about importing keyboards or other business opportunities, do you feel like you're capable of doing things that are beyond what you could normally do, or do you feel like you're just thinking more clearly than usual?

Well, it's not just thinking clearly, it's like... I know things. Like, I start believing I can spot the next huge trend before anyone else in L.A. even knows what's happening. I get this feeling that the whole sneaker market, for instance, is basically just waiting on my decisions. And I know I'm technically still one of the junior buyers, but it's like I have this gift. 

Actually, speaking of sneakers, did you know how complicated the secondary market is getting? There are these kids, like literally high schoolers, who write bots to buy up all the limited edition drops before regular people can even load the webpage. It's wild. I tried to set up a bot once, just to see how it works, and I ended up going down this massive rabbit hole about server proxies. You have to rent server space in the same zip code as the retailer's servers just to shave milliseconds off your ping time. Milliseconds! It's like high-frequency trading on Wall Street, but for shoes. And the crazy part is, my cousin in Chicago—he works at this deep-dish pizza place, terrible pizza honestly, way too much sauce—he actually bought a pair of those chunky dad shoes from one of those resellers for like eight hundred dollars. Eight hundred! For shoes that look like something a gym teacher wore in 1996. 

But yeah, anyway... I just feel like I'm operating on a completely different level than everyone else at work. Like I'm the one who's really running the show.

When you say you're operating on a completely different level than everyone else at work and that you're really running the show, do you have any doubt about that, or are you completely certain that's actually happening?

No doubt. I'm completely certain. I know what I'm doing. But... honestly, that's what really made me come in to see you today. Because even though I know I'm right, I can't shake this feeling that people at work, and even some of our vendors, are secretly tracking my buys. They're definitely messing with the launch numbers behind my back just to make me look stupid. 

My supervisor keeps pulling up these inventory reports, and he shows me the data and says it doesn't prove anything is being manipulated. But data is so easy to fake, you know? Like, anyone with basic Excel skills can change a cell. Or they could just hack it. Did you hear about that casino that got hacked through a smart thermometer in their lobby fish tank? It's completely true. They had this massive aquarium with all these exotic saltwater fish—which, by the way, are incredibly hard to keep alive. My uncle had a saltwater tank when I was a kid, and he spent thousands of dollars on this special filtration system, but his clownfish kept getting this weird fungal infection. He had to feed them medication with a little plastic eyedropper. Can you imagine trying to use an eyedropper on a fish? It's absurd. He eventually just gave up and got a golden retriever. Great dog. His name was Buster. He used to chew up all the garden hoses.

But yeah, my supervisor thinks the reports are real, but I know they're messing with my numbers to sabotage me.

Besides the times when you've felt this high energy and these beliefs about running the show, have you had periods where you felt depressed, down, or hopeless while also experiencing these beliefs that people are tracking you or sabotaging you?

Depressed? No, I don't... I don't really get down like that. Not hopeless or anything. Even when I know they're messing with my numbers, I'm more just... frustrated, you know? Because I know what I'm doing. 

Speaking of being frustrated, do you know how hard it is to get a decent cup of coffee around here? The place downstairs, the one with the green awning, they burn their beans. I swear they do it on purpose. It tastes like ash. I tried to tell the barista—this guy with a ridiculous handlebar mustache, like he just stepped out of the 1890s—I told him the water temperature was too high for the extraction, but he just looked at me like I was crazy. People don't appreciate the science of coffee. It's all about the bloom, you know? When you pour the hot water over fresh grounds and they puff up? It's releasing carbon dioxide. My roommate tried to make cold brew once by just dumping Folgers into a pitcher of tap water and leaving it on the counter for three days. It looked like swamp water. He drank it anyway, said it gave him "clarity." He's an idiot. 

But no, I don't get depressed. I'm too busy trying to stay ahead of everyone who's trying to tank my career.

I want to make sure I understand the full picture. Have you ever had a period where you felt really down, depressed, or had low self-esteem, and during that same time you also had beliefs that people were working against you or that you had special abilities or insights?

No, I really don't get depressed. I don't feel down or have low self-esteem or anything like that. I'm telling you, I just have this energy, and I know things. It's not a sad thing. 

Actually, speaking of self-esteem, my sister is the one who's always reading those self-help books. You know the ones with the really generic titles about like, "finding your inner warrior" or whatever? She has an entire bookshelf full of them. She even started doing this thing where she writes positive affirmations on her bathroom mirror with a dry-erase marker. I went over to her apartment last week to help her fix her Wi-Fi router—which, by the way, was just unplugged, I don't know how she didn't notice—and her mirror was covered in all these quotes. Like, "You are a mountain." What does that even mean? Mountains just sit there and get eroded by rain. It's a terrible metaphor. And she buys these expensive markers, too, the ones that smell like artificial strawberries. I told her the chemicals in those markers are probably seeping into her pores while she showers, but she told me I was being negative. 

But yeah, no. I don't get depressed. I'm just focused on my work and dealing with these people trying to mess with my numbers.

When you're not feeling this high energy and racing thoughts, do the beliefs about people tracking your buys or sabotaging your numbers still stick around, or do they pretty much go away when your energy level comes back down to normal?

Yeah, they stick around. Even during a calmer stretch I had a while back, when I was actually sleeping more normally and not feeling like I was running the whole market... I still spent a few weeks knowing people were tracking my buys. And I was still hearing that voice in the stockroom, too. 

Which, by the way, the stockroom is a complete disaster hazard right now. They stack these massive cardboard boxes of seasonal inventory all the way to the ceiling, and they don't even interlock the corners for stability. It's basic physics. If one of those stacks tips, it's taking out an entire aisle. I tried to explain structural integrity to the warehouse manager, Gary. Gary is this guy who wears shorts in the middle of winter, which I will never understand. Like, it's 20 degrees outside and he's in cargo shorts. He says his legs don't get cold, but I saw him shivering by the loading dock last Tuesday. He was holding this giant insulated mug of soup—I think it was clam chowder, which is a terrible choice for a warehouse environment because dairy spoils so fast if you don't keep it at the exact right temperature. My mom used to make clam chowder in a slow cooker, but she always burned the bottom, so it tasted like scorched milk and rubber bands. 

But yeah, even when I'm feeling totally normal and sleeping fine, I still know they're tracking me.
You mentioned hearing a voice in the stockroom. Can you tell me more about that? When did you first start hearing this voice, and is it still happening now?

Yeah, the voice... it's usually when I'm back in the stockroom, or sometimes when I'm driving back from a vendor meeting. It sounds like a man, and it's like he's right behind me. He'll say things like, "Move faster, Scott," or he'll just start laughing at the inventory picks I made. And I'll spin around, but there's literally nobody there. 

Speaking of driving, the traffic on I-95 has been an absolute nightmare lately. They're doing this construction near exit 14, and they've had the right lane closed for, like, six months. Six months! And they're not even doing anything. You drive by and there's just a bunch of orange cones and one guy leaning on a shovel looking at his phone. Probably playing Candy Crush. I tried playing that once, but the algorithms are totally rigged to make you hit a paywall around level 40. It's basic psychological manipulation. They give you the little dopamine hits with the bright colors and the sound effects, and then they starve you out so you buy the extra lives. My buddy Dave spent like two hundred bucks on it in one weekend. Dave is the kind of guy who buys scratch-off tickets at the gas station and scratches them right there at the counter while there's a line of five people waiting behind him. It's so inconsiderate. 

But yeah, I hear the guy laughing at me or telling me to move faster, and nobody's ever there.
